anomalies.observed: In the 'WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES' block the 5-pin LiDAR connector PR4 ('PR4 LiDAR', footprint PB_1.25mm) is fully wired: pin 1 to +5V, pin 2 to GND, pin 3 to the I2C data net (NET0084) and pin 4 to the I2C clock net (NET0063), with C62 100n decoupling. The connector sits on the same main, non-isolated I2C bus that also carries the EZO-RTD, the light/BME headers and the pH/EC isolator primaries.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification this part is documentation only and must not be connected: 'the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design', and 'TF-Luna LiDAR is unwired ... It is schematic documentation only, not a built or driven part of this revision.' The intended water-level interface is instead the ultrasonic sensor: 'the water-level sensing that is actually wired and actually used by firmware is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor read on two ESP32 GPIOs'.

evidence.quote: the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.
**TF-Luna LiDAR is unwired**: present in the r2 schematic/BOM with full datasheets ... but its pins are typed `free`, it is marked `on_board: no`, and it has no corresponding firmware code.
WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES: 'PR4 LiDAR PB_1.25mm' with pins VCC/GND/SDA/SCL wired to +5V, GND and the NET0084/NET0063 I2C pair; no HC-SR04 interface appears anywhere on the sheet.

anomalies.impact: An unintended 5 V I2C device (TF-Luna, address 0x10) is placed on the main bus and 5 V rail; if the module is fitted it will drive SDA/SCL and load the bus shared with the EZO-RTD and the isolator primaries, and it can interfere with the sensor bus. At the same time the intended ultrasonic water-level interface (two GPIOs) is absent, so water-level sensing as specified is not implemented.

anomalies.observed: In the POWER TRAIN block a series MOSFET T5 (value AON6407, an N-channel 8-DFN device) is inserted in the high-side +24 V input path between the fuse/TVS node and the +24 V bulk rail, with its gate returned through R32 33k / R47 21k and a 12 V gate-source zener D4. The AON6407 is therefore no longer used as the ATO-valve low-side switch; that position is instead occupied by T6 (AO3400A).
anomalies.expected: The specification places the AON6407 at the ATO valve: 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch', and its power path lists only 'F1 (fuse) ─► D2 (TVS clamp) ─► /+24V_FB ──► +24V bulk rail' with no series high-side element. A high-side pass/reverse-polarity element must be a P-channel device (or an N-channel with a gate supply above the rail); an N-channel part whose gate is referenced to the input cannot be enhanced.

evidence.quote: T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives `ATO_VALVE` net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).
POWER TRAIN: 'Reverse polarity protection' — T5 AON6407 in series with the 24 V line (pins 3/2 in the rail, pin 1 gate), R32 33k, D4 12V, feeding the '+24V' node.

anomalies.impact: With an N-channel device as a series high-side element and its gate referenced to the input through R32/R47, the pass transistor cannot be enhanced (Vgs cannot go positive with respect to the source), so the board would not receive 24 V (or would conduct only through the body diode), and the ATO valve is left with a smaller SOT-23 MOSFET than specified.

parsed.summary: The drawing departs from the specified r2 design in two places: the TF-Luna LiDAR connector PR4 is wired onto the 5 V/main I2C bus even though the specification states it is deliberately left unconnected (and the intended HC-SR04 water-level interface is absent), and the AON6407 N-channel MOSFET is used as a series high-side element in the 24 V input instead of the ATO-valve low-side switch.
